target_zone_range.evidence_basis: Hays County field collection between Five Mile Dam and Blanco Shoals; Bandera County riparian documentation explicitly lists little walnut; Comal County historical national-champion record near Fischer documents the species.
target_zone_range.guardrail: Exact county evidence only; no broad-range inference.

morphology.look_here_first: Start with fruit size and leaflet narrowness. Little walnut is the smallest-fruited local walnut: fruits about 1.4–2.3 cm and nuts about 1.1–1.7 cm, with 17–25 narrow leaflets. It is usually a shrub or small tree rather than a massive canopy tree.
diagnostic_traits: shrub or small tree, generally to about 10 m
nut about 1.1–1.7 cm with longitudinal grooves and relatively smooth surfaces between grooves

confusers.separator: J. major has fewer, broader leaflets and larger 2–3.5 cm fruits; J. nigra has much larger 3.5–8 cm fruits and a coarsely warty nut surface.

caveat: Flora of North America notes intermediates among central Texas Juglans, so atypical trees should be checked with fruit/nut characters as well as leaflet count.
